claim: B lymphocytes use B cell receptors (BCRs) to recognize antigens.
source: B lymphocytes use B cell receptors (BCRs) to recognize antigens.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in immunology presented as background information.

claim: BCR complex comprises a membrane-bound immunoglobulin (mIg) and a noncovalently linked heterodimer composed of Igα and Igβ in 1:1 stoichiometry of mIg: Igα/β.
source: BCR complex comprises a membrane-bound immunoglobulin (mIg) and a noncovalently linked heterodimer composed of Igα and Igβ in 1:1 stoichiometry of mIg: Igα/β (Tolar et al., 2005; Hombach et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Antigen engagement induces phosphorylation of immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs) in Igα/β by the Src family kinase Lyn.
source: Antigen engagement induces phosphorylation of immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs) in Igα/β by the Src family kinase Lyn, resulting in the triggering of signaling cascades (Pierce and Liu, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The molecular mechanism through which BCR extracellular antigen binding signal is transmitted across the membrane to the BCR intracellular ITAMs remains unclear.
source: However, remain unclear is the molecular mechanism through which BCR extracellular antigen binding signal is transmitted across the membrane to the BCR intracellular ITAMs for the purpose of B cell activation.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The 'conformational change model' proposes that through a series of conformational changes within the BCR complex, the interaction of antigen with the extracellular domain of mIg is transduced to the intracellular domain of BCR.
source: 'Conformational change model' has been proposed to explain the initiation of B cell activation, in which it is supposed that through a series of conformational changes within the BCR complex, the interaction of antigen with the extracellular domain of mIg is transduced to the intracellular domain of BCR (Harwood and Batista, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research proposing this model.

claim: Previous studies support the conformational change model by investigating FRET within BCR cytoplasmic domains.
source: several previous studies support this conformational change model by investigating fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) within BCR cytoplasmic domains (Tolar et al., 2005), FRET between plasma membrane and Igα cytoplasmic domain (Lee and Tolar, 2013), FRET between membrane and cytoplasmic domain of mIgG (Chen et al., 2015) upon antigen engagement, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Binding of antigen led to a conformational change in the BCR cytoplasmic domains from a closed to an open form.
source: In these studies, binding of antigen led to a conformational change in the BCR cytoplasmic domains from a closed to an open form (Tolar et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Antigen binding causes an increased distance between membrane and Igα but not Igβ.
source: an increased distance between membrane and Igα but not Igβ (Lee and Tolar, 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Antigen binding causes dissociation of mIgG cytoplasmic tail from cell membrane.
source: dissociation of mIgG cytoplasmic tail from cell membrane (Chen et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The Cμ4 portion in mIgM (and Cγ3 portion in mIgG) of the extracellular domain of BCR is both required and sufficient for antigen-binding induced BCR oligomerization and signaling.
source: it is also reported that the Cμ4 portion in mIgM (and Cγ3 portion in mIgG) of the extracellular domain of BCR is both required and sufficient for antigen-binding induced BCR oligomerization and signaling, suggesting antigen engagement triggered the Cμ4 domain of IgM-BCR (or Cγ3 domain of IgG-BCR) into an orientation in which BCRs are accessible for oligomerization (Tolar et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: IgM-BCR activation was dependent on mechanical force and exhibited a multi-threshold dependence.
source: IgM-BCR activation was dependent on mechanical force and exhibited a multi-threshold dependence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous studies.

claim: The activation of IgG-BCR only required a low threshold of less than 12 pN.
source: In contrast, the activation of IgG-BCR only required a low threshold of less than 12 pN (Wan et al., 2015; Wan et al., 2018; Wang and Ha, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR can be successfully expressed and labeled in 293T cells.
source: Dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR can be successfully expressed and labeled in 293T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR can bind with HIV-1 gp120 antigen (V51 monomer) as WT VRC01-IgM-BCR.
source: Dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR can bind with HIV-1 gp120 antigen (V51 monomer; Wang et al., 2018a) as WT VRC01-IgM-BCR (Figure 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Stimulation by V51 trimer induced similar calcium influx signal in untagged and dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells.
source: the stimulation by V51 trimer (A foldon trimerization domain of T4 fibritin was fused to the C terminus of V51 for the production of V51 trimer) (Wang et al., 2018a) induced similar calcium influx signal in untagged and dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Dually tagged VRC01-IgG-BCR expressed in 293T cells or A20II1.6 B cells exhibited comparable function as WT VRC01-IgG-BCR.
source: Similarly, dually tagged VRC01-IgG-BCR expressed in 293T cells or A20II1.6 B cells exhibited comparable function as WT VRC01-IgG-BCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The binding of antigen lowered the FRET efficiency between N terminus and Cμ2 domain in VRC01-IgM-BCR.
source: The results showed that the binding of antigen lowered the FRET efficiency between N terminus and Cμ2 domain as measured by the quantification of donor recovery after acceptor bleaching using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (TIRFM) (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D using TIRFM-based acceptor photobleaching FRET.

claim: The reduction of FRET signal indicated an increased spatial distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain upon antigen engagement.
source: The reduction of FRET signal indicated an increased spatial distance between these two sites upon antigen engagement.
evidence: This is an inference based on the FRET data showing reduced FRET efficiency.

claim: Decreased FRET between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within IgM heavy chain resulted from V51 monomer antigen engagement was obtained using FLIM-FRET measurement.
source: Decreased FRET between these two sites within IgM heavy chain resulted from V51 monomer antigen engagement was similarly obtained, as indicated by the increased fluorescence lifetime of CoA 488 (donor chromophore) and thus reduced FLIM-FRET signal after antigen binding (Figure 2E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E–H using FLIM-FRET method.

claim: The reduced FRET signal within the ectodomain of BCR also occurred in A20II1.6 B cells.
source: We also repeated the same FRET measurement via acceptor photobleaching method in A20II1.6 B cells to confirm that the reduced FRET signal within the ectodomain of BCR also occurred in B cells (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The increased distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain of IgM-BCR upon antigen binding suggested that the antigen-induced conformational change might originate at antigen binding site.
source: The increased distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain of IgM-BCR upon antigen binding suggested that the antigen-induced conformational change might originate at antigen binding site.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the FRET data.

claim: Antigen binding caused significant lower FRET between CoA 488 and ReAsH in cells expressing dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCRs.
source: Under the same experimental condition as above, antigen binding caused significant lower FRET between CoA 488 and ReAsH in cells expressing dually tagged VRC01-IgM-BCRs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: FRET signal between CoA 488 and ReAsH in singly tagged VRC01-IgM-BCRs expressing cells was very low, and no FRET change was observed between these two fluorophores upon antigen engagement.
source: Meanwhile, FRET signal between CoA 488 and ReAsH in singly tagged VRC01-IgM-BCRs expressing cells was very low, and no FRET change was observed between these two fluorophores upon antigen engagement (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The alteration of FRET between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within IgM heavy chain generated by antigen-BCR interaction was mainly attributed by the increase of intramolecular distance between these two sites, rather than the intermolecular distance changes.
source: suggesting the alteration of FRET between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within IgM heavy chain generated by antigen-BCR interaction was mainly attributed by the increase of intramolecular distance between these two sites, rather than the intermolecular distance changes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of FRET signals in dually tagged vs. singly tagged BCRs.

claim: Intermolecular FRET accounted for about 1/3 of the detected intramolecular FRET signal.
source: We found that intermolecular FRET accounted for about 1/3 of the detected intramolecular FRET signal, and antigen engagement significantly decreased intramolecular FRET, but not intermolecular FRET (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Antigen engagement significantly decreased intramolecular FRET, but not intermolecular FRET.
source: We found that intermolecular FRET accounted for about 1/3 of the detected intramolecular FRET signal, and antigen engagement significantly decreased intramolecular FRET, but not intermolecular FRET (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Inverse correlation between the FRET efficiency and the mean fluorescent intensity (mFI) of p-Igα was observed.
source: Inverse correlation between the FRET efficiency and the mean fluorescent intensity (mFI) of p-Igα was observed (Figure 2J)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The spatial distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg is closely associated with the strength of B cell activation.
source: indicating the spatial distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg is closely associated with the strength of B cell activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between FRET efficiency and p-Igα recruitment.

claim: Crystal structures of antigen-antibody complex indicate that antigen binding does not transmit conformational changes to the membrane-proximal regions of Ig molecule.
source: Since the crystal structures of antigen-antibody complex indicate that antigen binding does not transmit conformational changes to the membrane-proximal regions of Ig molecule (Metzger, 1974; Metzger, 1992)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: No FRET change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within soluble VRC01-IgM upon antigen binding was found using acceptor photobleaching FRET method.
source: Through acceptor photobleaching FRET method, we found no FRET change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within soluble VRC01-IgM upon antigen binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: No change of spatial distance between N terminus and Cμ2 domain in soluble VRC01-IgM after antigen engagement was observed using FLIM-FRET method.
source: Similarly, using FLIM-FRET method, no change of spatial distance between these two sites in soluble VRC01-IgM after antigen engagement was observed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–G.

claim: Distance between N terminus and Cγ2 domain in VRC01-IgG-BCR remained unchanged after interacting with V51 monomer antigen.
source: In comparison with IgM-BCR, distance between N terminus and Cγ2 domain in VRC01-IgG-BCR remained unchanged after interacting with V51 monomer antigen, as illustrated by the unaltered FRET between CoA 488 label at the N terminus and ReAsH label at Cγ2 of IgG heavy chain (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: GGM-BCR exhibited the similar FRET change after antigen stimulation as IgM-BCR.
source: The results showed that GGM-BCR exhibited the similar FRET change after antigen stimulation as IgM-BCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing GGM-BCR and IgM-BCR.

claim: No significant conformational change occurred in antigen-stimulated MMG-BCR, resembling the behavior of IgG-BCR.
source: In contrast, no significant conformational change occurred in antigen-stimulated MMG-BCR, resembling the behavior of IgG-BCR (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: IgG cytoplasmic tail slightly decreased the basal FRET efficiency between CoA 488 and ReAsH in VRC01-BCR without antigen-binding.
source: In addition, we found that IgG cytoplasmic tail slightly decreased the basal FRET efficiency between CoA 488 and ReAsH in VRC01-BCR without antigen-binding (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D), while the difference was not significant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction effect between Ig cytoplasmic tail and antigen engagement on FRET between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2).
source: Moreover, two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction effect between Ig cytoplasmic tail and antigen engagement on FRET between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2), indicating that Ig cytoplasmic tail significantly affected the antigen-induced conformational change within mIg of BCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Antigen-binding significantly increased distance between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2) within mIg only in the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail.
source: Two-way ANOVA with Sidak's correction for multiple comparisons confirmed that antigen-binding significantly increased distance between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2) within mIg only in the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail, while the presence of IgG cytoplasmic tail did not significantly increase the basal distance between these two sites of BCR without antigen-binding (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: IgM- and IgG-BCR exhibit distinct conformational change within the mIg heavy chain upon antigen binding and such difference is dependent on the cytoplasmic tail of mIg.
source: All these results suggested that IgM- and IgG-BCR exhibit distinct conformational change within the mIg heavy chain upon antigen binding and such difference is dependent on the cytoplasmic tail of mIg.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data comparing IgM-BCR, IgG-BCR, MMG-BCR, and GGM-BCR.

claim: VRC01-BCRs with tetracysteine tag in Igβ were expressed and site-specifically labeled.
source: Confocal microscopy of transfected 293T cells showed that VRC01-BCRs with tetracysteine tag in Igβ were expressed and site-specifically labeled (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Both WT and tagged VRC01-BCR can bind with V51 monomer.
source: Both WT and tagged VRC01-BCR can bind with V51 monomer (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: V51 trimer can induced calcium influx in tagged VRC01-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells.
source: V51 trimer can induced calcium influx in tagged VRC01-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells, although the calcium signals in tagged VRC01-IgM-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells showed a little less sustained signal than cells expressing untagged VRC01-IgM-BCR (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: No FRET change between mIg and Igβ in IgM-BCR complex occurred upon antigen binding.
source: The result showed that no FRET change between these two sites occurred upon antigen binding, suggesting no change of spatial distance occurred between mIg and Igβ in IgM-BCR complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B,C.

claim: A decreased intermolecular FRET efficiency between Alexa Fluor 647 label at Fcγ fragment of IgG heavy chain and ReAsH label in extracellular domain of Igβ was found in VRC01-IgG-BCR upon stimulation by membrane antigen.
source: We found a decreased intermolecular FRET efficiency between Alexa Fluor 647 label at Fcγ fragment of IgG heavy chain and ReAsH label in extracellular domain of Igβ measured by acceptor photobleaching FRET method in 293T cells (Figure 4B–C), indicating an increased spatial distance between mIg heavy chain and Igβ in VRC01-IgG-BCR upon the stimulation by membrane antigen.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B–C.

claim: Membrane V51 monomer antigen caused a FRET reduction between mIg heavy chain and Igβ in VRC01-IgG-BCR as confirmed by FLIM-FRET measurement.
source: As a further validation, FLIM-FRET measurement confirmed that membrane V51 monomer antigen similarly caused a FRET reduction between these two sites in VRC01-IgG-BCR (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D–G.

claim: Increased distance between mIg heavy chain and Igβ was confirmed in tagged VRC01-IgG-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells after binding with antigen.
source: Increased distance between mIg heavy chain and Igβ was also confirmed in tagged VRC01-IgG-BCR expressing A20II1.6 B cells after binding with antigen (Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: FRET efficiency between mIg heavy chain and Igβ was found to be inversely correlated with the level of synaptic recruitment of p-Igα.
source: Moreover, FRET efficiency between these two sites was found to be inversely correlated with the level of synaptic recruitment of p-Igα (Figure 4I)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: The spatial distance between extracellular domains of mIg and Igβ is closely associated with the strength of B cell activation.
source: indicating the spatial distance between extracellular domains of mIg and Igβ is closely associated with the strength of B cell activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between FRET efficiency and p-Igα recruitment.

claim: Spatial distance between mIg heavy chain and Igβ in IgG cytoplasmic tail carrying VRC01-MMG-BCR increased upon antigen engagement.
source: In line with the change observed in antigen-stimulated VRC01-IgG-BCR, spatial distance between mIg heavy chain and Igβ in IgG cytoplasmic tail carrying VRC01-MMG-BCR increased upon antigen engagement, as illustrated by the decreased FRET efficiency.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing MMG-BCR with IgG-BCR.

claim: VRC01-GGM-BCR possessing IgM cytoplasmic tail resembled the behavior of VRC01-IgM-BCR, in which the distance between mIg and Igβ remained unaffected after antigen activation.
source: By contrast, VRC01-GGM-BCR possessing IgM cytoplasmic tail resembled the behavior of VRC01-IgM-BCR, in which the distance between mIg and Igβ remained unaffected after antigen activation (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The presence of IgG cytoplasmic tail significantly increased the basal FRET efficiency between ReAsH and AF647 in VRC01-BCR without antigen binding.
source: In addition, we observed that the presence of IgG cytoplasmic tail significantly increased the basal FRET efficiency between ReAsH and AF647 in VRC01-BCR without antigen binding (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction effect between Ig cytoplasmic tail and antigen engagement on FRET between mIg and Igβ.
source: Moreover, two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction effect between Ig cytoplasmic tail and antigen engagement on FRET between mIg and Igβ, indicating that Ig cytoplasmic tail significantly affected the antigen-induced conformational change in the spatial relationship between mIg and Igβ.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Antigen-binding significantly increased the distance between mIg and Igβ only in the presence of IgG cytoplasmic tail.
source: Two-way ANOVA with Sidak's correction for multiple comparisons confirmed that antigen-binding significantly increased the distance between mIg and Igβ only in the presence of IgG cytoplasmic tail, while IgG cytoplasmic tail significantly decreased the basal distance between these two molecules (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The antigen-induced conformational change within mIg heavy chain might be transmitted to Igα/β, decreasing proximity between mIg and Igβ of IgG-BCR.
source: these results suggested that the antigen-induced conformational change within mIg heavy chain might be transmitted to Igα/β, decreasing proximity between mIg and Igβ of IgG-BCR.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Conformational change in the spatial relationship between mIg and Igβ is dependent on the cytoplasmic tail of mIg and is associated with the initial intracellular signaling in activated B cell.
source: In addition, conformational change in the spatial relationship between mIg and Igβ is dependent on the cytoplasmic tail of mIg and is associated with the initial intracellular signaling in activated B cell.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data.

claim: When BCRs encounter antigens, the mobility of BCRs will be reduced followed by BCR oligomerization and the formation of BCR microclusters.
source: When BCRs encounter antigens, the mobility of BCRs will be reduced followed by BCR oligomerization and the formation of BCR microclusters (Tolar et al., 2005; Harwood and Batista, 2010; Mattila et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2010a; Liu et al., 2010b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: BCR is an extraordinary receptor that can efficiently discriminate the biochemical and biophysical features of an antigen, such as the stiffness of the substrates presenting the antigen.
source: BCR is an extraordinary receptor that can efficiently discriminate the biochemical and biophysical features of an antigen, such as the stiffness of the substrates presenting the antigen (Wan et al., 2013; Zeng et al., 2015; Shaheen et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2018b) and mechanical force signals delivered by antigen (Wan et al., 2015; Wan et al., 2018; Natkanski et al., 2013; Nowosad et al., 2016; Spillane and Tolar, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Several crystal structures of antibodies in the presence of soluble antigens indicate that antigen binding seems incapable of propagating significant conformational changes to membrane-proximal regions of Ig.
source: However, several crystal structures of antibodies in the presence of soluble antigens indicate that antigen binding seems incapable of propagating significant conformational changes to membrane-proximal regions of Ig (Davies and Metzger, 1983; Davies et al., 1990; Metzger, 1978).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The interaction between cytoplasmic tail and cell membrane is necessary for the antigen-induced conformational change in cytoplasmic domain of BCR.
source: In addition, according to our published studies, the interaction between cytoplasmic tail and cell membrane is necessary for the antigen-induced conformational change in cytoplasmic domain of BCR (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous research.

claim: Extracellular conformational change-mediated oligomerization of the BCR requires the WTxxST motif in the transmembrane region of mIg.
source: It is also reported that extracellular conformational change-mediated oligomerization of the BCR requires the WTxxST motif in the transmembrane region of mIg (Tolar et al., 2009), which is lacked in soluble Ig.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Interaction between BCR complex and cell membrane might be crucial for conformational changes within ectodomains of BCR upon antigen engagement.
source: These findings indicate that interaction between BCR complex and cell membrane might be crucial for conformational changes within ectodomains of BCR upon antigen engagement.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on previous findings.

claim: Decreased proximity between N terminus and Cμ2 domain were discovered in both 293T cells and A20II1.6 B cells, indicating the independence of the conformational change on downstream signaling after antigen stimulation.
source: Notably, decreased proximity between this two sites were discovered in both 293T cells and A20II1.6 B cells, indicating the independence of the conformational change on downstream signaling after antigen stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the conformational change occurs in both cell types.

claim: Distance change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain observed in this study might involve stretching or bending of the hinge region.
source: Since these two regions locate across the hinge region linking Fab and Fc fragment of mIg, distance change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain observed in this study might involve stretching or bending of the hinge region.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the FRET data.

claim: The level of conformational change (as indicated by the FRET efficiency) within mIg of IgM-BCR was positively associated with the strength of B cell activation.
source: Interestingly, the level of conformational change (as indicated by the FRET efficiency) within mIg of IgM-BCR was positively associated with the strength of B cell activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between FRET efficiency and B cell activation markers.

claim: Conformational change within mIg was dependent on the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail.
source: We also found that conformational change within mIg was dependent on the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data comparing different BCR constructs.

claim: In the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail, antigen engagement induced conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg of IgM-BCR, while greater conformational change was associated with higher activation level in B cell.
source: Combining all these findings, we speculated that in the absence of IgG cytoplasmic tail, antigen engagement induced conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg of IgM-BCR, while greater conformational change was associated with higher activation level in B cell.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg of antigen-bound IgM-BCR was then transmitted to membrane-proximal domain, while this transduction was achieved in IgG-BCR without change of spatial distance between N terminus and Cγ2 domain.
source: Potentially, conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg of antigen-bound IgM-BCR was then transmitted to membrane-proximal domain, while this transduction was achieved in IgG-BCR without change of spatial distance between N terminus and Cγ2 domain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Extracellular antigen signal transmitted to membrane-proximal region might trigger local conformational change in Fc domain of mIg, inducing an orientation to expose a clustering interface on the Cμ4 (or Cγ3) domain.
source: Extracellular antigen signal transmitted to membrane-proximal region might trigger local conformational change in Fc domain of mIg, inducing an orientation to expose a clustering interface on the Cμ4 (or Cγ3) domain (Tolar et al., 2009) (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation combining the current data with previous findings.

claim: Increased spatial distance between mIg and Igα/β of IgG-BCR might generated from the dissociations of IgG cytoplasmic tail and Igα from the plasma membrane.
source: Increased spatial distance between mIg and Igα/β of IgG-BCR might generated from the dissociations of IgG cytoplasmic tail and Igα from the plasma membrane (Lee and Tolar, 2013; Chen et al., 2015) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation combining the current data with previous findings.

claim: The extracellular domains of Igα/β preferentially recognize the Fc region of IgM compared with IgG.
source: Meanwhile, it has been reported that the extracellular domains of Igα/β preferentially recognize the Fc region of IgM compared with IgG (Radaev et al., 2010), potentially inhibit the dissociation between mIg and Igβ in IgM-BCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Reduced proximity between extracellular domains of mIg and Igβ might induce the increased distance between cytoplasmic domains of mIg and Igα/β heterodimer, facilitating the formation of 'umbrella opening form' in cytoplasmic domains of antigen-activated BCR.
source: In line with previous findings, reduced proximity between extracellular domains of mIg and Igβ might induce the increased distance between cytoplasmic domains of mIg and Igα/β heterodimer, facilitating the formation of 'umbrella opening form' in cytoplasmic domains of antigen-activated BCR (Tolar et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation combining the current data with previous findings.

claim: Agonist and antagonist will induce distinct conformational change of GPCR, indicating different conformational changes within GPCR might trigger different physiological functions.
source: Agonist and antagonist will induce distinct conformational change of GPCR, indicating different conformational changes within GPCR might trigger different physiological functions (Vafabakhsh et al., 2015; Olofsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on GPCRs.

claim: IgG cytoplasmic tail enhances antigen-induced B cell activation.
source: the enhancement of IgG cytoplasmic tail on the antigen-induced B cell activation (Chen et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2010b; Wakabayashi et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2) domain is only required for IgM-BCR (or IgG-BCR equipped with IgM cytoplasmic tail) to transmit antigen-binding signal to membrane-proximal domain.
source: One possible explanation is that conformational change in the spatial relationship between N terminus and Cμ2 (or Cγ2) domain is only required for IgM-BCR (or IgG-BCR equipped with IgM cytoplasmic tail) to transmit antigen-binding signal to membrane-proximal domain, inducing an orientation to expose a clustering interface on the Cμ4 (or Cγ3) domain (Tolar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: IgG cytoplasmic tail lowers the threshold of mechanical force to induce IgG-BCR activation.
source: This hypothesis seems to be consistent with the previous findings that IgG cytoplasmic tail lowers the threshold of mechanical force to induce IgG-BCR activation (Wan et al., 2015; Wan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous research.

claim: IgG cytoplasmic tail might lower the threshold of B cell activation through bypassing the required conformational change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg in IgM-BCR.
source: Considering that the mechanical force might be closely related with the conformational change, it is reasonable to speculate that IgG cytoplasmic tail might lower the threshold of B cell activation through bypassing the required conformational change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain within mIg in IgM-BCR.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation combining the current data with previous findings.

claim: Spatial distance change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain of mIg in IgM-BCR could be interpreted as an inhibitory mechanism.
source: Another possible explanation is that spatial distance change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain of mIg in IgM-BCR could be interpreted as an inhibitory mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Antigen-induced conformational change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain might inhibit further BCR activation through an unexplored mechanism.
source: Antigen-induced conformational change between N terminus and Cμ2 domain might inhibit further BCR activation through an unexplored mechanism.
